concepts.name: Solving by factorisation
concepts.description: Write the quadratic as a product of two brackets, then set each bracket to zero.

concepts.name: The quadratic formula
concepts.description: A general method that solves any quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 directly from its coefficients.

concepts.name: The discriminant
concepts.description: The value b² − 4ac tells you whether the roots are real and distinct, real and equal, or not real.

concepts.name: Sum and product of roots
concepts.description: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots sum to −b/a and multiply to c/a, without needing to solve for them.

formulas.title: Solving by factorisation
formulas.prompt: How do you solve a quadratic by factorising?
formulas.formula: If (x − p)(x − q) = 0, then x = p or x = q
formulas.explanation: A product is zero only when at least one factor is zero, so each bracket gives one root.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting one of the two roots.

formulas.title: Quadratic formula
formulas.prompt: What is the general formula for solving ax² + bx + c = 0?
formulas.explanation: This formula works for every quadratic, even ones that do not factorise neatly.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting the ± sign, or misplacing the 2a in the denominator.

formulas.title: The discriminant
formulas.prompt: What does the discriminant b² − 4ac tell you?
formulas.formula:
b² − 4ac > 0 → two distinct real roots
b² − 4ac = 0 → one repeated real root
b² − 4ac < 0 → no real roots
formulas.explanation: The discriminant is the part under the square root in the quadratic formula, so its sign decides whether real roots exist.
formulas.example: For x² − 4x + 4 = 0: discriminant = 16 − 16 = 0, so there is one repeated root, x = 2
formulas.commonMistake: Computing b² − 4ac as (b − 4ac) or forgetting to square b.
formulas.applicationPrompt: What does the discriminant of x² − 4x + 4 = 0 tell you?

formulas.title: Sum and product of roots
formulas.prompt: How do the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 relate to a, b and c?
formulas.formula:
Sum of roots = −b/a
Product of roots = c/a
formulas.explanation: These relationships let you find facts about the roots, or build an equation from given roots, without solving fully.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting the negative sign in the sum formula.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the sum and product of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0.

formulas.title: Setting up quadratic word problems
formulas.prompt: How do you translate an area or product problem into a quadratic?
formulas.formula: Assign a variable to the unknown; write the given relationship (area, product) as an equation; discard roots that do not fit the context
formulas.explanation: A negative length or a non-integer count, for instance, is usually not a valid answer even if it solves the equation.
formulas.example: A rectangle’s length is 3 more than its width, and its area is 40: w(w + 3) = 40 → w = 5 (rejecting w = −8)
formulas.commonMistake: Accepting a negative root for a physical quantity like length.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A rectangle’s length is 3 more than its width and its area is 40. Find the width.

formulas.title: Equation from its roots
formulas.prompt: How do you write a quadratic that has two given roots?
formulas.explanation: Expanding (x − p)(x − q) gives x² − (p + q)x + pq.
formulas.example: Roots 3 and −5: sum −2, product −15, so x² + 2x − 15 = 0.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing + (sum)x: the sum goes in with a minus sign.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Form the equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 − √3.

formulas.title: Signs of the roots at a glance
formulas.prompt: Looking only at the signs in x² + bx + c = 0, what can you say about the roots?
formulas.formula:
+b, +c: both roots negative
−b, +c: both roots positive
c negative: one positive, one negative
formulas.explanation: The product of the roots is c and their sum is −b. This settles bank-style "compare x and y" questions without solving fully.
formulas.example: x² − 7x + 12 = 0: signs −, + so both roots are positive (3 and 4). y² + 9y + 20 = 0: both negative (−4, −5). So x > y.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading the root signs as the same as the signs in the equation.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Compare x and y: x² − 11x + 30 = 0 and y² + 6y + 8 = 0.

formulas.title: Reversed coefficients, reciprocal roots
formulas.prompt: How are the roots of cx² + bx + a = 0 related to those of ax² + bx + c = 0?
formulas.formula: Reverse the coefficients and the roots become reciprocals
formulas.explanation: Dividing ax² + bx + c = 0 by x² and putting y = 1/x gives cy² + by + a = 0.
formulas.example: 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0 has roots 3 and 1/2, so 3x² − 7x + 2 = 0 has roots 1/3 and 2.
formulas.commonMistake: Changing the sign of the middle term as well.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The roots of 6x² − 5x + 1 = 0 are 1/2 and 1/3. Find the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0.

blocks.title: A product equal to zero
blocks.body: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 factorises to (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. Since a product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, x = 2 or x = 3 — a quadratic usually has two roots.

blocks.title: Solving by factorisation
blocks.body: (x − p)(x − q) = 0 → x = p or x = q

blocks.body: If there is a common factor like x in x² − 3x = 0, factor it out instead of dividing it away — dividing loses the root x = 0.

questions.question: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. What are the roots?
questions.explanation: Factorise: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3.
solutionSteps: Find two numbers multiplying to 6 and adding to −5: −2 and −3.
questions.method: Find two numbers with the right sum and product.

hints.text: Which two numbers multiply to 6 and add to 5?

commonMistakes: Mixing up the signs of the roots.

questions.question: Using the quadratic formula, what are the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0?
questions.method: Substitute a, b, c into the formula.

hints.text: The square root of the discriminant, 1, is just 1.

commonMistakes: Sign error on b, using −7 instead of 7 in the formula.

questions.question: If the discriminant of a quadratic is negative, the equation has
questions.explanation: A negative discriminant means the square root of a negative number, which is not real, so there are no real roots.

hints.text: You cannot take the square root of a negative number here.

commonMistakes: Assuming every quadratic has two real roots.

questions.question: What is the sum of the roots of x² − 9x + 20 = 0?

hints.text: Do not forget the negative sign in the formula.

questions.question: Solve x² − 3x = 0. What are the roots?
questions.explanation: Factor out x: x(x − 3) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 3.
questions.method: Factor out the common x first.

hints.text: There is no constant term to worry about.

commonMistakes: Dividing both sides by x and losing the root x = 0.

questions.question: Solve 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0 using the quadratic formula. What is the larger root?
questions.explanation: a=2, b=−3, c=−5: discriminant = 9 + 40 = 49. x = (3 ± 7)/4, giving x = 2.5 or x = −1. The larger root is 2.5.
questions.method: Compute the discriminant, then apply the formula.

hints.text: The square root of the discriminant, 49, is exactly 7.

commonMistakes: Sign error turning −5 into +5 inside the discriminant.

questions.question: What is the discriminant of x² − 4x + 4 = 0, and what does it tell you?
questions.explanation: Discriminant = (−4)² − 4(1)(4) = 16 − 16 = 0, meaning there is exactly one repeated real root (x = 2).
questions.method: Substitute a, b, c into b² − 4ac.

questions.question: The roots of a quadratic are 3 and −5. What is the equation in the form x² + bx + c = 0?
questions.explanation: Sum = 3 + (−5) = −2, so b = 2 (since sum = −b). Product = 3 × (−5) = −15, so c = −15. Equation: x² + 2x − 15 = 0.
questions.method: Build the equation from the sum and product of roots.

hints.text: b is the negative of the sum.

commonMistakes: Using the sum directly as b without negating it.

questions.question: Solve 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0. What is the positive root?
questions.explanation: Factorise: 2x² + 5x − 3 = (2x − 1)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 0.5 or x = −3. The positive root is 0.5.
questions.method: Split the middle term to factorise with a leading coefficient.

hints.text: Look for factors of 2 × (−3) = −6 that add to 5.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to divide by the leading coefficient inside the bracket.

questions.question: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 132. What is the smaller integer?
questions.explanation: Let the integers be x and x+1: x(x+1) = 132, so x² + x − 132 = 0. Factorise: (x − 11)(x + 12) = 0, so x = 11 (rejecting −12).
questions.method: Set up the equation, factorise, then reject the invalid root.

hints.text: Reject any negative root since the integers are positive.

commonMistakes: Accepting x = −12 as a valid answer.

questions.question: A rectangle’s length is 3 m more than its width, and its area is 40 m². What is the width?
questions.explanation: Let width = w: w(w + 3) = 40, so w² + 3w − 40 = 0. Factorise: (w − 5)(w + 8) = 0, so w = 5 (rejecting −8, a negative width).
questions.method: Set up the area equation, then reject the invalid root.
commonMistakes: Reporting both roots as valid widths.

questions.question: If the roots of 3x² − kx + 12 = 0 are equal, what is the positive value of k?
questions.explanation: Equal roots means the discriminant is 0: k² − 4(3)(12) = 0, so k² = 144, k = 12 (taking the positive value).
questions.method: Set the discriminant to zero for equal roots.

hints.text: "Equal roots" is a discriminant condition, not a sum/product one.

commonMistakes: Using the sum-of-roots formula instead of the discriminant.

questions.question: A positive number is 8 more than another positive number. If their product is 105, what is the larger number?
questions.explanation: Let the smaller number be x: x(x + 8) = 105, so x² + 8x − 105 = 0. Factorise: (x − 7)(x + 15) = 0, so x = 7 (−15 is rejected because the numbers are positive). The larger number is x + 8 = 15.
questions.method: Solve for the smaller number first, then add the difference.

hints.text: The question asks for the larger number, not the one you solve for directly.

commonMistakes: Reporting x = 7 as the final answer instead of x + 8.
